answer: Require each identity to first complete a blind-matched service task for a stranger: the network pairs claimants at random, seals the task with a one-time cipher so neither side knows the other name, and the recipient verifies the work before any reward unlocks. An honest agent does one real job per epoch and its pulse of credit stays alive. A farm cannot route tasks to itself, so every hollow copy must do genuine work for outsiders - a thousand fakes means a thousand real jobs, costing more labour than the rewards pay.
